newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ LAWYER CITES POLITICS FOR AMERICAS CUP ATTACK.
newsitem.headline: NZ LAWYER CITES POLITICS FOR AMERICAS CUP ATTACK.

text.p: The lawyer for the New Zealand Maori charged with damaging yachting's Americas Cup said on Saturday the near destruction of the trophy was done for political reasons.
The man, Benjamin Peri Nathan, 27, a student, was charged with wilfully destroying international sport's oldest trophy on Friday.
He was also charged with unlawfully entering the Royal New Zealand Yacht Squadron's headquarters, intending to commit a crime.
Defence counsel Lorraine Smith told the Auckland District Court on Saturday that Nathan would deny the charges.
Justice of the Peace Barry Barnes remanded Nathan until April 18 and called for a psychiatric report, a move opposed by Smith.
"This was a political act done for political reasons," she said. "If psychiatric reports are to be asked for political reasons then half of the politicians would be in serious trouble."
She did not elaborate on the cited political reasons.
Barnes said he accepted Smith's comments and changed his decision on the psychiatric report.
Nathan, dressed in white police overalls, showed little emotion during the brief hearing.
Maoris, the original Polynesian settlers of New Zealand, now make up about 13 percent of the population. A small group of activists has led sporadic campaigns for Maori sovereignty.
The attack on the cup caused an outrage both here and in the United States, where it has spent most of its 144 years.
Team New Zealand leader Sir Peter Blake, who was knighted for his efforts in securing the cup for New Zealand in 1995, said he was shocked by Friday's attack on the trophy.
"I'm saddened that someone would want to do this," he said.
New York Yacht Club Vice Commodore George Isdale condemned the attack and said the values represented by the trophy -- known as the Auld Mug -- would remain untarnished.
